stories.h: Odion Ighalo says he has paid tithe since his first ₦15,000 salary, sparks debate
stories.p: Former Super Eagles striker Odion Ighalo has reportedly said he has never missed paying tithe since his first salary in 2005, even when he earned $642,000 a month in Saudi Arabia. His comments have divided opinion online.
body: Former Super Eagles striker Odion Ighalo has started a lively online debate after speaking about his long commitment to paying tithes.
## What he said

In a podcast-style interview, reportedly shared on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, Ighalo said he began paying tithe in 2005 when he received his first professional salary of ₦15,000, after his pastor introduced him to the practice, and that he has not missed it since. He admitted that the habit became harder when his income grew. When he was earning a reported $642,000 a month in Saudi Arabia, about ₦900 million at today's exchange rate, he said he thought about it for around a month before deciding to continue paying 10 per cent. He said some friends had questioned his decision, but he stood by it.
## Background

Ighalo, 37, played for clubs including Watford and Manchester United before moving to Saudi Arabia, where he became one of the best-paid African players. He was top scorer at the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations and has long spoken publicly about his Christian faith.
## How people reacted

Opinion was divided. Many Christians praised his faith and discipline and said his success was a blessing. Others argued that giving such large sums to churches was unnecessary and that the money could do more good if given directly to people in need. Some said it was his personal choice and others should respect it.
## Why it matters
Tithing is a frequent topic of debate in Nigeria, where churches play a large role in public life and some pastors have faced criticism over their wealth.

stories.h: Deposed Ipetumodu monarch sues Adeleke to stop appointment of successor
stories.p: Oba Joseph Oloyede, removed as Apetumodu of Ipetumodu after his conviction in the US for fraud, has reportedly asked an Osun High Court to stop Governor Ademola Adeleke from filling the stool. The case was adjourned to 21 January 2027.
body: The deposed Apetumodu of Ipetumodu in Osun State, Oba Joseph Oloyede, has gone to court to stop Governor Ademola Adeleke from appointing a new traditional ruler for the town.
## The case

According to reports, Oloyede filed a motion at the Osun State High Court in Ile-Ife asking the court to restrain the governor and other officials from filling the stool until his main case is decided. In the application, dated 16 September 2026, he argued that he was not formally told of any wrongdoing before he was removed, and challenged the legality of his deposition. Members of a branch of the town's ruling house joined him as claimants. The defendants include the governor, the state Attorney-General, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, local chiefs and Ife North Local Government.
## What happened in court

Proceedings stalled on Monday, 2 November, after some defendants said they had not received hearing notices. Justice Dapo Adeniji adjourned the case to 21 January 2027 and ordered that fresh notices be served.
## Background

Oloyede was removed from the throne after he was convicted in the United States on charges related to tax fraud and money laundering. Governor Adeleke reportedly signed the order removing him in May 2026.
## What happens next
The court will hear the case in January. Until then, it is not clear whether the state will go ahead with appointing a new monarch.
more: He says he was not told of any wrongdoing before his removal.

stories.h: US reportedly carries out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on eve of midterms
stories.p: US officials say American forces carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, in response to Iranian missile fire at US assets. Iranian state media reported explosions, while Iran claimed it captured two US drones.
body: The United States military has reportedly carried out limited strikes on Qeshm Island, a strategic Iranian island near the Strait of Hormuz, on Monday, 2 November 2026, the eve of the US midterm elections.
## What happened

According to US officials quoted in reports, the operation was a defensive response after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) fired surface-to-air missiles at US assets. Iranian state media confirmed several explosions on the island. Officials reportedly said it was one of a series of low-profile strikes carried out in recent weeks, kept quiet to avoid signalling a return to full-scale fighting. Separately, the IRGC claimed it had intercepted and captured two US drones south of Qeshm.
## Why Qeshm matters

Qeshm is the largest island in the Persian Gulf and is said to hold Iranian anti-ship missiles, sea mines and drones in underground tunnels. Its position near the Strait of Hormuz, through which a large share of the world's oil passes, makes it militarily important.
## Diplomacy continues

The strikes came as Qatar leads indirect talks between the two sides. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, described the talks as active, and on Monday Iran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US met its conditions. US Vice President JD Vance reportedly said there had been progress, but warned that Iran remains unpredictable and that President Donald Trump would keep both military and diplomatic options open.
## Why it matters

Oil prices rose slightly after reports of the strikes, with Brent crude trading at about $105 a barrel. Higher oil prices affect Nigeria's revenue and fuel costs around the world. The conflict between the US and Iran began on 28 February.
more: US officials called it a defensive response to Iranian missile fire.

stories.h: US to remove South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA duty-free trade scheme
stories.p: The US says it will remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act from 1 January 2027, accusing both of practices that break the scheme's rules. South Africa says it will support affected industries.
body: The United States plans to remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), its main duty-free trade programme for African countries, from 1 January 2027.
## What the US said

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Monday, 2 November 2026, that President Donald Trump intends to end the two countries' participation in the scheme. According to reports, Greer said the President found that both governments were engaging in practices inconsistent with AGOA's eligibility rules, including barriers to American trade and investment and actions that threaten US security and foreign policy interests in the region.
## South Africa's response

South Africa's trade ministry said it would support the sectors affected and would keep pursuing trade and investment with the United States. It said AGOA remains important but is not the whole of the economic relationship between the two countries.
## What is at stake

AGOA, enacted in 2000, gives eligible African countries duty-free access to the US market for thousands of products. South Africa has been its largest beneficiary, exporting about $1.7 billion worth of goods under the scheme in 2025, mainly car parts, citrus fruit and wine. Rwanda's main exports include coffee and minerals.
## Background

The Trump administration has taken a series of steps against South Africa, accusing its government of persecuting white South Africans, a claim Pretoria rejects. Nigeria remains an AGOA beneficiary, although its exports under the scheme are dominated by oil. Trade experts say the decision is a warning to other African countries that eligibility can be withdrawn.
more: The suspension takes effect on 1 January 2027.
South Africa exported about $1.7 billion under AGOA in 2025.

stories.h: Atiku's campaign says Umrah will not win Tinubu a second term
stories.p: A spokesman for Atiku Abubakar's campaign has reportedly said President Tinubu's Umrah trip will not secure his re-election, arguing that voters will judge him on the cost of living. Tinubu said he went to give thanks, as he did before the 2023 election.
body: The campaign of African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar says President Bola Tinubu's recent Umrah in Saudi Arabia will not guarantee him a second term.
## What was said

Speaking on a television politics programme on Monday night, 2 November 2026, Phrank Shaibu, director of strategic communication for the ADC presidential campaign council, reportedly said political mandates cannot be won through religious display. He argued that pilgrimage should be a personal matter, not something publicised as a national event by political supporters, and said Nigerians would make their choice in 2027 based on the cost of living rather than prayers abroad. Asked whether Atiku would have joined Tinubu if invited, he said the former vice-president had supported Tinubu's earlier trips to Mecca. He also claimed Atiku was in a strong position in the North.
## The President's side

Tinubu left Abuja for Makkah on 29 October. He described the trip as a chance to seek divine guidance, wisdom and resilience, and said that before the 2023 election he had performed Umrah and promised to return to give thanks if his prayers were answered. During the visit he was granted the rare privilege of entering the Kaaba, where he said he prayed for peace, unity and prosperity for Nigeria. The Presidency has rejected claims that the trip was for medical reasons.
## Background

The trip has drawn comment across the political spectrum. Former senator Dino Melaye challenged Tinubu to a Quran recitation contest, while Oyo governor Seyi Makinde asked the Presidency to explain the purpose of the journey. APC supporters have welcomed the visit and the honour extended by the Saudi leadership.
more: The ADC says voters will judge Tinubu on the cost of living.

stories.h: Video of Catholic priest leading campaign song for Obi and Kwankwaso goes viral
stories.p: A video showing a Catholic priest leading his congregation in an Igbo song praising Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso's party during a Sunday service has gone viral. It adds to debate over religious leaders taking sides ahead of 2027.
body: A video of a Catholic priest leading worshippers in a song backing NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi and his running mate Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has spread widely on social media.
## What the video shows

In the clip, reportedly filmed during a Sunday service, the priest leads the congregation in an Igbo song saying the party of Obi and Kwankwaso is better, and the worshippers sing along. The priest's name and the location of the church have not been confirmed. The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), which ratified Obi as its presidential candidate in May, shared the video.
## Religious leaders and politics

The video comes as religious leaders across Nigeria increasingly declare support for or against candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. According to reports, a separate bishops' conference has endorsed President Bola Tinubu for a second term, while an Islamic cleric was reported to have urged Muslims to vote along religious lines. Last week, a Catholic bishop warned politicians against trying to manipulate the electoral system, and a priest urged Nigerians to collect their voter cards instead of complaining.
## How people reacted

Obi's supporters celebrated the video, while critics said churches should not be used for partisan campaigns and warned that such displays could deepen religious and ethnic divisions. Others said priests, like all citizens, are entitled to their political views.
## Background
Electoral rules prohibit the use of places of worship for political campaigns, although enforcement has historically been rare. The Catholic Church has not publicly commented on the video.
more: The priest led an Igbo song praising Obi and Kwankwaso's party.

stories.h: Atedo Peterside says Tinubu's reforms are making the rich richer and the poor poorer
stories.p: Investment banker Atedo Peterside has reportedly said the government's economic reforms are benefiting wealthier Nigerians with investments while low-income workers are worse off. He said his concern is for the more than 130 million Nigerians who are poor.
body: Investment banker and IBTC founder Atedo Peterside says the Tinubu administration's economic reforms are widening the gap between rich and poor Nigerians.
## What he said

Speaking in a television interview on Monday night, 2 November 2026, Peterside reportedly said that whether the reforms are working depends on who is asked. He said upper-middle-class Nigerians with investments in the stock market are probably better off than they were three years ago, while low-income workers with little savings who struggle to eat two meals a day and pay their bills are a lot worse off. He admitted that his own investment income had risen, but said his concern was for the 130 to 140 million Nigerians who are poor and getting poorer.
## Background

The government removed the petrol subsidy and unified the exchange rate in 2023, moves that pushed up prices but which it says were needed to rescue the economy. Officials point to falling inflation, which dropped to 14.63 per cent in September, rising foreign reserves and a stock market that hit a record high last week. Critics say these gains have not yet reached ordinary households, many of whom still struggle with high food and transport costs.
## Political debate

The state of the economy is a central issue in the 2027 campaign. Opposition candidates say the reforms have made life harder, while the government says it is cushioning the poor through cash transfers and credit schemes.
more: Peterside says investors are better off, low-income workers worse off.

stories.h: Tanzania head to Uyo early for Super Eagles AFCON qualifier
stories.p: Tanzania's national team is reportedly arriving early in Uyo to prepare for their 2027 AFCON qualifier against the Super Eagles on Friday, 13 November. The sides meet again in Dar es Salaam four days later.
body: Tanzania's national team, the Taifa Stars, are set to arrive early in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, ahead of their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Nigeria's Super Eagles, according to reports.
## The fixtures

Nigeria will host the matchday three game at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on Friday, 13 November 2026. The two teams will meet again four days later in Dar es Salaam for the matchday four fixture.
## Tanzania's preparations

Head coach Miguel Gamondi reportedly wants extra time for his players to get used to conditions in Nigeria before the game. He has named a 24-man squad split evenly between 12 home-based players and 12 who play abroad.
## Background

The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations will be co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. The Super Eagles need good results in the double-header to stay on course for the tournament. Uyo has become the Super Eagles' main home ground in recent years and is known for its passionate crowds. The confederation recently confirmed Nigerian Samson Adamu as its General Secretary and voted to return the Nations Cup to a two-year cycle.
## What happens next
The Super Eagles are expected to open camp in Uyo next week, with fans looking forward to two important results.
more: Nigeria host Tanzania in Uyo on Friday, 13 November.
The return game is in Dar es Salaam four days later.

stories.h: Government opens new round of free vocational training with ₦30,000 monthly stipend
stories.p: The federal government has reportedly opened applications for Batch C of its TVET initiative, offering free training in trades such as solar installation, plumbing and fashion design, plus a ₦30,000 monthly stipend. Applications are free on the official portal.
body: The federal government has opened applications for the third batch of its Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) initiative, which offers free skills training and a monthly stipend, according to reports on Monday, 2 November 2026.
## What is on offer

The programme, coordinated by the Federal Ministry of Education, provides free vocational training at accredited technical colleges, government institutions and registered private centres across the country. Participants receive ₦30,000 a month throughout their training. Trades on offer reportedly include solar installation, plumbing, fashion design and car repairs.
## Two training options

Applicants can choose a six-month short-term certificate course aimed at beginners, school leavers and people without formal qualifications, or a one-year vocational education and innovation course for those with previous education or informal training in a trade.
## How to apply

Applications are free and are made through the official TVET portal. No closing date has been announced, so applicants are advised to watch for official updates and to avoid anyone asking for money to register.
## Background

The initiative was launched to tackle youth unemployment and the country's skills gap by training young Nigerians in practical trades that are in demand. Earlier batches attracted large numbers of applicants. The scheme is one of several government programmes aimed at easing hardship, alongside cash transfers and consumer credit.
more: Participants get ₦30,000 a month during training.
Courses last six months or one year.
Applications are free on the official portal.

stories.h: Police officers feared dead as bandits ambush bus heading to Zamfara APC primary
stories.p: Bandits ambushed a bus carrying police officers on the Sokoto–Gusau road in Zamfara State on Monday. The officers were travelling to provide security for an APC senatorial primary, and some are feared dead while others were reportedly abducted.
body: Several police officers are feared dead after suspected bandits attacked a bus carrying them along the Sokoto–Gusau road in Zamfara State on Monday, 2 November 2026.
## What happened

The officers were travelling in a state mass transit bus, known locally as Bazamfara, towards Gusau, the state capital. According to police sources, they were on their way to provide security for the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for the Zamfara North senatorial district, which was taking place in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. Sources said some officers were killed in the ambush and others were abducted by the attackers. The exact number of casualties had not been confirmed at the time of reporting.
## Official response

The spokesman for the police zone covering the area reportedly confirmed the attack, but said he was in hospital and would issue an official statement later. The identities of the victims have not been released.
## Background

Zamfara is one of the states worst affected by banditry in north-west Nigeria, with frequent attacks on travellers, villages and security personnel. Police officers are often deployed to provide security at party primaries and campaign events, and several political gatherings have been attacked in recent weeks as the 2027 elections approach. In neighbouring Niger State, gunmen abducted 14 Islamiyya students and their teacher at the weekend.
## Primary result

The primary went ahead despite the attack. The APC later declared Sahabi Ya'u Kaura the winner of the fresh Zamfara North senatorial primary, held after a court invalidated the earlier exercise. He reportedly polled 49,176 votes, ahead of Tijjani Kaura with 9,628 and Abdullahi Sani Shinkafi with 6,206, winning in all four local government areas.
## What happens next
Security agencies are expected to launch an operation to rescue the abducted officers, and the police are expected to release casualty figures.

stories.h: Gunmen abduct 14 Islamiyya students and their teacher on Niger farm
stories.p: Police in Niger State say suspected bandits abducted 14 Islamiyya students and their teacher while they were harvesting maize on a farm in Rafi Local Government Area. Police corrected earlier reports that 50 pupils were taken.
body: Suspected bandits have abducted 14 students of an Islamic school and their teacher in Rafi Local Government Area of Niger State, police have confirmed.
## What happened

The attack happened at about 12.30pm on Saturday, 31 October 2026, in Tungan-Bako village near Pandogari. According to the police, the students were helping their teacher harvest maize on his farm when armed men stormed the area and took them away.
## Police statement

The spokesman for the Niger State Police Command, Wasiu Abiodun, confirmed the incident on Monday, 2 November. He said the number of students abducted was 14, correcting earlier reports that about 50 pupils had been seized. He said a joint team of security forces had been deployed to rescue the victims and that further updates would be given.
## Background

Rafi and nearby local government areas in Niger State have suffered repeated attacks by armed groups in recent years, including mass abductions from schools and villages. Kidnapping for ransom remains a serious problem across north-west and north-central Nigeria, and farmers are often targeted during the harvest season. On the same day the abduction was confirmed, bandits ambushed a bus carrying police officers in neighbouring Zamfara State.
## What happens next
Families and community leaders are calling for the quick and safe release of the students.
more: The students were harvesting maize on their teacher's farm.
Police say 14 students were taken, not 50.
A joint rescue operation is under way.

stories.h: Eedris Abdulkareem releases new song asking Seyi Tinubu to plead with his father
stories.p: Veteran rapper Eedris Abdulkareem has reportedly released a new music video in which he addresses Seyi Tinubu, asking him to beg his father, President Tinubu, to ease Nigerians' hardship. He also criticised the new tax law and the electoral system.
body: Veteran rapper Eedris Abdulkareem has released a new song with a pointed political message for President Bola Tinubu, this time delivered through the President's son, Seyi Tinubu.
## The song

In a music video posted on Instagram on Monday, 2 November 2026, Eedris reportedly addresses Seyi directly, asking him to plead with his father on behalf of Nigerians. The lyrics contrast the President's role as a good father to his own family with what the rapper describes as hardship for ordinary Nigerians. According to reports, the song also takes aim at the National Assembly over the newly passed tax law and criticises the electoral system.
## Background

Eedris, best known for his 2004 hit 'Jaga Jaga', has used music to criticise Nigerian governments for more than two decades. In 2025 he released a song critical of the Tinubu government, which the broadcasting regulator restricted on air. On Monday he also denied claims that he had joined the APC, accusing Isaac Fayose of hypocrisy for saying so. Seyi Tinubu has become a visible figure in his father's re-election campaign, and the Presidency has defended the government's reforms, saying they are needed to fix the economy.
## How people reacted

The video drew strong reactions online. Many fans praised the rapper for speaking up about the cost of living, while supporters of the President accused him of playing politics ahead of the 2027 elections.
## What happens next
Neither Seyi Tinubu nor the Presidency had responded publicly at the time of reporting.
more: Eedris addresses Seyi Tinubu directly in the lyrics.
The song also criticises the new tax law.
The Presidency has not responded.

stories.h: Government credit agency launches SPARK scheme for buying food and solar on credit
stories.p: The Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation has reportedly launched SPARK, a scheme to help Nigerians buy food, solar systems and other household goods on credit, including through a USSD code. It says over 351,000 people have accessed more than ₦53.5 billion in credit so far.
body: The Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP), a federal government agency, has launched a new scheme called SPARK to help Nigerians buy essential goods on credit, according to reports on Monday, 2 November 2026.
## What SPARK offers

The scheme is designed to let people buy items such as food, solar power systems and other household needs without paying the full amount upfront. It also aims to support Nigerian businesses and manufacturers by boosting demand for locally made goods. Reports say Nigerians will be able to access the service through a USSD code, which works on basic phones without internet access.
## The numbers so far
CREDICORP says it has facilitated more than ₦53.5 billion in consumer credit for over 351,000 Nigerians since it began operations, and that women make up about 59 per cent of beneficiaries.
## A loan, not a grant

Applicants are being reminded that SPARK is a loan that must be repaid, not free money. People are advised to check the official terms, use only official channels and beware of fraudsters who may pretend to offer access to the scheme for a fee.
## Background

CREDICORP was set up in 2024 as part of President Tinubu's plan to make consumer credit more widely available, so that working Nigerians can buy goods such as cars, homes and appliances and pay over time. Critics have questioned how many people can afford new debt at a time of high living costs, while supporters say affordable credit can ease pressure on household budgets.
more: SPARK lets people buy food and solar systems on credit.
Over 351,000 Nigerians have accessed ₦53.5 billion so far.
It is a loan that must be repaid.

stories.h: Young Ibadan boxer KBlaq dies after being stabbed during fight, suspect arrested
stories.p: A young boxer known as KBlaq has reportedly died after being stabbed during a fight at Olodo Garage in Ibadan on Sunday. A suspect is said to have been arrested and handed over to the police.
body: A fast-rising Nigerian boxer identified as Kehinde, popularly known as KBlaq, has reportedly died after being stabbed during a fight in Ibadan, Oyo State.
## What happened

According to reports on social media, the incident happened on Sunday, 1 November 2026, during a confrontation at Olodo Garage in Ibadan. He was said to have died shortly after he was attacked. The cause of the fight has not been made public.
## Arrest
A suspect was reportedly arrested and handed over to the police. The Oyo State Police Command had not issued a public statement on the case at the time of reporting.
## How people reacted
Friends and fans mourned the young boxer on social media and called on the police to ensure justice. Many described him as a promising talent whose career was just beginning.
## What happens next
Police are expected to investigate the incident and charge the suspect in court if there is enough evidence.
more: KBlaq reportedly died after a fight at Olodo Garage.
A suspect was said to have been handed to the police.
Friends and fans are calling for justice.

stories.h: UK and Nigeria agree three-year plan against visa fraud and illegal migration
stories.p: The UK and Nigeria have reportedly agreed a three-year programme to tackle organised immigration crime, covering visa fraud, document checks, deportations and data sharing. The plan grew out of President Tinubu's state visit to the UK in March.
body: The United Kingdom and Nigeria have agreed a three-year programme to tackle organised immigration crime, with details published by the UK Home Office, according to reports.
## What the plan covers

The programme targets criminal networks behind irregular migration and visa fraud. Both countries have committed to tighter border security and better verification of travel documents. They also agreed to deepen cooperation on returns of people with no right to stay, the sharing of data and extradition.
## How it came about

The programme was first announced during President Bola Tinubu's state visit to the UK in March 2026, when Nigeria's interior minister and the UK Home Secretary signed a joint statement. Officials from both countries agreed on next steps at their annual migration, justice and home affairs dialogue in London on 6 October, and a joint communiqué setting out the plan was published on 16 October.
## What it means for Nigerians

For genuine travellers, the plan is likely to mean stricter checks on documents used in visa applications. Officials say it should also make it harder for fraudsters who sell fake documents or promise people illegal routes to the UK.
## Background

The UK is one of the most popular destinations for Nigerian students and workers. The British government has been tightening its immigration rules, and this week dropped a plan to make some care workers wait 15 years for permanent settlement, while keeping a 10-year route for most lower earners.
more: The plan targets visa fraud and irregular migration.
It includes cooperation on returns and data sharing.
It was first announced during Tinubu's March state visit.

stories.h: Police reportedly arrest suspect over shooting death of 15-year-old Ghanaian boy Javits Frimpong in New York
stories.p: Police have reportedly made an arrest in connection with the shooting of Javits Frimpong, a 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was killed while walking to school in the Bronx, New York. Questions remain about what led to the shooting and whether others were involved.
body: Police have reportedly made an arrest in connection with the tragic shooting of Javits Frimpong, a 15-year-old Ghanaian teenager who was killed in the Bronx, New York.
The development reportedly came after officers spent much of the afternoon searching for suspected gang members believed to have been involved in the incident.
## What happened
Javits was shot and killed while walking to school in the Bronx last week. He had moved from Ghana about a year earlier to live with his father, Thomas Frimpong, in New York.
His father has said he believes bullying may have been behind the attack, and police have been looking into it as a possible motive.
## Grief and calls for justice

The killing has caused deep grief in the Ghanaian community and beyond. Students in the Bronx staged a walkout after his death, a memorial in his honour has continued to grow, and the Ghanaian government has vowed to pursue justice for the boy.
## Questions remain

Although one suspect is now reportedly in custody, several questions remain unanswered, including what exactly led to the shooting and whether other people were involved. The identity of the person reportedly arrested has not been officially confirmed.
Police investigations are expected to continue as officers try to piece together what happened and establish who was responsible.
## A life cut short
For Javits Frimpong's family, no arrest can bring back the young life that has been lost. At just 15 years old, he had so much of his future ahead of him.
The hope now is that a thorough investigation will uncover the truth and ensure that anyone found responsible is brought to justice.
more: Javits was shot while walking to school in the Bronx.
His father believes bullying may have been involved.
Ghana's government has vowed to pursue justice.

stories.h: Court orders arrest of Lagos NURTW chairman Sego over alleged contempt
stories.p: The National Industrial Court in Lagos has ordered the arrest of Lagos NURTW chairman Mustapha Adekunle, known as Sego, and the union's secretary, after they failed to appear to explain why they should not be jailed for contempt. The case arises from a dispute with tricycle operators.
body: The National Industrial Court in Lagos has ordered the arrest and detention of the Lagos State chairman of the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Mustapha Adekunle, popularly known as Sego, and the union's secretary, Usman Teslim.
## What the court said

Justice Isaac Essien gave the order on Monday, 2 November 2026, after the two officials failed to appear in court to show why they should not be sent to prison for contempt. According to reports, the judge described their conduct as brazen disobedience of court orders and warned that the authority of the courts must not be undermined. He directed the Lagos Commissioner of Police, the state commandant of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and other security agencies to arrest the two men and hand them over to the officer in charge of the Kirikiri Correctional Centre.
## Bailiff obstruction

The court also raised concern over an affidavit filed by its bailiff, who said he was prevented from serving court papers on 5 October by a security officer linked to one of the parties in the case. Justice Essien reportedly described the alleged obstruction as a dangerous development.
## Background

The case stems from a long-running dispute between commercial tricycle operators and the NURTW in Lagos over control of operations and levies. The union has been at the centre of several leadership and legal battles in the state in recent years. Sego and the union have not publicly responded to the order.
## What happens next
The officials can still appear before the court or challenge the order on appeal. It is not yet clear whether security agencies have acted on the directive.
more: The judge cited brazen disobedience of court orders.
Security agencies were told to hand the officials to Kirikiri.
The union has not yet responded.

stories.h: Iran says it could reopen Strait of Hormuz within two days if US meets its demands
stories.p: Iran has reportedly said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours if Washington accepts its conditions, including lifting oil sanctions and ending a naval blockade. Talks in Doha ended without a breakthrough.
body: Iran says it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most important oil shipping routes, within 48 hours if the United States accepts its conditions for ending the war between the two countries.
## What Iran said

Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday, 2 November 2026, that Tehran had shortened an earlier seven-day proposal to two days, and reportedly described this as a sign of good faith. He said reopening the waterway and returning to negotiations depended on Washington agreeing to Iran's demands, and that messages were still being exchanged through mediators.
## Iran's conditions

According to reports, Iran wants an end to the war across the Middle East, the release of its frozen assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade of its ports. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has also called for a new transit arrangement for ships passing through the strait, agreed between Iran and Oman, and fewer US troops in the region.
## Background

The two countries have been in conflict for about eight months. Iranian and Qatari negotiators held three days of talks in Doha aimed at reaching a deal, but they ended without a breakthrough. On Sunday, President Donald Trump told a rally that the US might eventually have to give Iran 'the hammer', and Iran's army said it was ready for a long war.
## Why it matters

A large share of the world's oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz. Disruption there affects global oil prices, which matters for Nigeria's earnings from crude oil and for fuel costs around the world.
more: Iran cut its proposed timeline from seven days to two.
It wants sanctions lifted and the naval blockade ended.
Talks in Doha ended without a breakthrough.

stories.h: Car dealer Moses Auto says fire destroyed vehicles worth over ₦700 million
stories.p: Car dealer Moses Auto Car Care says a fire at his business destroyed his own cars worth more than ₦500 million and customers' cars worth over ₦200 million. Many people online sympathised and urged businesses to take insurance and fire safety seriously.
body: A Nigerian car dealer known online as Moses Auto Car Care has described the heavy losses he suffered after a fire swept through his car lot.
## What he said

In comments shared on Monday, 2 November 2026, the dealer reportedly said that cars worth more than ₦500 million belonging to him were destroyed in the fire. He added that customers' vehicles worth over ₦200 million were also burnt, including cars that buyers had already paid for but had not yet collected. He did not say what caused the fire or when exactly it happened.
## How people reacted

Many social media users expressed sympathy and prayed for him to recover from the loss, with some praising him for staying strong. Others said the incident showed the importance of insurance, which many Nigerian businesses do not take, and of basic fire safety equipment such as alarms and sprinklers. Some asked how the customers who had paid for cars would be compensated.
## Background

Fires at markets, shops and car lots cause large losses in Nigeria every year, often linked to electrical faults or poor safety measures. Fire services frequently urge business owners to install extinguishers and alarms and to insure their goods.
## What happens next
It is not yet clear whether the business was insured or how the dealer plans to settle with affected customers.
more: His own cars worth over ₦500 million were destroyed.
Customers' cars worth over ₦200 million were also burnt.
People online urged businesses to take insurance seriously.

stories.h: Odumodublvck claims his song made Declan Rice famous in Nigeria
stories.p: Rapper Odumodublvck has reportedly claimed that Nigerians did not know Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice until he released a song about him. Many fans mocked the claim, pointing out that Rice was already a well-known England player.
body: Rapper Odumodublvck has sparked amused reactions online after claiming he introduced England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice to Nigerians.
## What he said

In comments shared on Monday, 2 November 2026, the rapper reportedly said that before he sang about Rice, nobody in Nigeria knew him, and that Rice blew up after the song, after which Arsenal discovered and signed him. He presented the claim as proof of how his music connects football and music fans.
## The song

Odumodublvck released his hit 'Declan Rice' in 2023, and it became one of the most popular Nigerian rap songs of that year, helping to make him one of the country's best-known young rappers. Rice, who was then captain of West Ham United and already an England international, joined Arsenal in 2023 in a British record transfer.
## How people reacted

Many fans mocked the claim, saying football followers in Nigeria knew Rice long before the song and that it was the rapper who benefited from the player's name, not the other way round. Others said he was joking or simply promoting himself, while some called it harmless banter.
## Background
Odumodublvck is known for bold statements and a confident persona, which have helped keep him in the spotlight. Arsenal is one of the most widely supported English clubs in Nigeria.
more: The rapper says Rice blew up after his song.
His hit 'Declan Rice' came out in 2023.
Fans mocked the claim online.

stories.h: Kolu tells Carter Efe to stop spoiling his name, explains missed Ghana trip
stories.p: Content creator Kolu has reportedly accused Carter Efe of damaging his reputation, saying he skipped a trip to Ghana with him to perform at a paid show in Abuja because he has a family to feed.
body: Content creator Kolu has publicly called out fellow creator and streamer Carter Efe, accusing him of tarnishing his name.
## What Kolu said

In a video shared on Monday, 2 November 2026, Kolu reportedly explained why he did not follow Carter Efe on a recent trip to Ghana. He said his decision had nothing to do with any personal grudge, but that he chose to attend a show in Abuja because he needed money to take care of his family. He suggested that he would not have been paid if he had gone to Ghana, and asked Carter Efe to stop spoiling his name.
## Background

Kolu and Carter Efe have had a public on-and-off relationship for several years, with disagreements regularly spilling onto social media. Earlier this year, Kolu reportedly asked Carter Efe for a loan to help bail fellow entertainer Portable, which Carter Efe declined. In June, Carter Efe claimed he had sent Kolu money on several occasions and denied abandoning him. Both creators attended the wedding of streamers Peller and Jarvis in August.
## How people reacted

Social media users were divided. Some said Kolu seized every chance to attack Carter Efe, while others said Carter Efe should treat him better. Many simply asked what was really going on between the two.
## What happens next
Carter Efe has not yet responded publicly.
more: Kolu says he chose a paid show in Abuja over the Ghana trip.
He accused Carter Efe of spoiling his name.
Carter Efe has not responded.

stories.h: President Tinubu seen kissing the sacred Black Stone during Umrah in Makkah
stories.p: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has been seen kissing the Black Stone, known as Al-Hajar Al-Aswad, while performing Umrah in Makkah, Saudi Arabia. Photos show him at the eastern corner of the Kaaba, surrounded by security officials.
body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has been seen kissing the sacred Black Stone, known as Al-Hajar Al-Aswad, while performing Umrah in the holy city of Makkah, Saudi Arabia.

Photos from the visit show the President, dressed in white, leaning into the silver frame that holds the stone as Saudi security officers stand by. Another photo shows him with members of his delegation in the courtyard of the Grand Mosque.
## About the Black Stone
The Black Stone sits at the eastern corner of the Kaaba, inside the Grand Mosque, and holds deep religious significance for Muslims around the world.
Kissing the stone is a practice associated with Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and many pilgrims seek the chance to do so whenever they visit the holy site.
## A spiritual journey
For Muslims, Umrah is a spiritual journey marked by prayer, worship and personal reflection.
The moment has also drawn attention to the religious side of Nigeria's leader as he performs one of Islam's important acts of worship.
## Over to you
What are your thoughts on this moment from President Tinubu's visit to Makkah?
more: The Black Stone is at the eastern corner of the Kaaba.
Kissing it follows the practice of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
Tinubu was performing Umrah in Makkah.

stories.h: Ned Nwoko asks public to stop death rumours about Regina Daniels, threatens legal action
stories.p: Senator Ned Nwoko has appealed to Nigerians to stop spreading false reports about the death and health of his estranged wife, actress Regina Daniels. He said she needs compassion to recover and that his team is documenting false posts for legal action.
body: Senator Ned Nwoko has made a public appeal for people to stop spreading false stories about his estranged wife, Nollywood actress Regina Daniels, including rumours that she has died.
## What he said

In a statement on social media on Monday evening, 2 November 2026, Nwoko asked fans, bloggers and social media commentators to give Regina some breathing space. He said she had been through more than many people realise and that what she needs most now is love, support and the chance to recover. He said the appeal was also for the sake of their children, who he said are well cared for and deserve to see their mother supported. He added that whatever difficulties the marriage has faced, her well-being has always mattered to him, and that this was a time for compassion, not judgement.
## Warning to rumour spreaders

Nwoko said he would not tolerate the deliberate spread of false information about Regina, especially made-up reports about her death, health or personal circumstances. He said his team was documenting such publications and that those responsible would be held to account through the proper legal channels.
## Background

Regina Daniels and Nwoko married in 2019 and have two sons. Their marriage has been the subject of public disputes this year, and the two are now described as estranged. In a video shared on her recent birthday, the actress gave fans a glimpse of health challenges she has been facing, which Nwoko referred to in his statement. Since then, several unverified claims about her condition have spread online.
## How people reacted
Many fans welcomed the statement and prayed for the actress's recovery, while others urged bloggers to be more careful with stories about people's health.
more: Nwoko says Regina needs compassion and space to heal.
His team is documenting false reports for legal action.
He says their children are well cared for.

stories.h: Obi's camp denies viral report that he broke his neck in gym accident
stories.p: Peter Obi's spokesman has reportedly dismissed as false a viral claim that the NDC presidential candidate was hospitalised after breaking his neck in a gym. He said Obi travelled abroad on Sunday for an international engagement.
body: The campaign of Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has rejected a viral social media report claiming that he had been hospitalised after breaking his neck in a gym accident.
## What the camp said

Obi's spokesman, Idris Zekeri, reportedly described the report and the photographs shared with it as completely false, in comments published on Monday, 2 November 2026. He said he was with the former Anambra governor on Sunday morning before Obi boarded a flight for an international engagement. Zekeri accused political opponents of making up the story to cause confusion among Obi's supporters ahead of the 2027 election.
## Background

False health claims about political figures have become common in the run-up to the January 2027 elections. Last week, the Presidency rejected claims by activist Omoyele Sowore that President Bola Tinubu travelled to Saudi Arabia for medical treatment, saying he went for Umrah. Fact-checkers have also debunked a clip that claimed Obi said he could not defeat Tinubu. Obi, who is running with Rabiu Kwankwaso, has been touring states including Nasarawa and Ebonyi in recent days.
## Why it matters

Observers say fake stories and doctored images can mislead voters, and INEC's chairman warned on Monday that cheap AI tools are making such material easier to produce. Voters are being urged to check claims with official sources before sharing them.
## What happens next
Obi is expected to resume campaigning when he returns from his trip.
more: Obi's spokesman says the broken-neck report is false.
He says Obi travelled abroad on Sunday.
The camp blames political opponents for the story.

stories.h: Wike says Rainbow Coalition critics cannot even unite their own families
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has said politicians who deny the Rainbow Coalition exists cannot hold their own families together, and urged FCT residents to vote for Tinubu. In Nasarawa, the APC has denied joining the coalition after a rival party candidate was named on its campaign council.
body: Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike has hit back at critics of the Rainbow Coalition, the cross-party alliance he leads in support of President Bola Tinubu's re-election.
## What Wike said

Speaking on Monday, 2 November 2026, at the commissioning of the Gwagwalada Civic Centre in Abuja and a meeting with APC and PDP stakeholders in the area council, Wike said some politicians who deny that the coalition exists have no capacity to hold their own families or communities together. He asked why leaders who once held opposing views could not work together for the public good, and praised local leaders in Gwagwalada for setting aside party differences. He urged residents to go to polling units, districts and communities and mobilise voters for Tinubu.
## Row in Nasarawa

In Nasarawa State, the APC faced criticism after Kabiru Dallah, the Zenith Labour Party candidate for Lafia/Obi federal constituency, was listed on its youth mobilisation committee. Some members alleged a hidden deal with the Rainbow Coalition. The state party secretary, Yarus Daguza, said Dallah's name had been removed and that the Nasarawa APC is not part of the coalition. Some members called on Governor Abdullahi Sule to dissolve the list and form a new campaign council, while supporters of losing governorship aspirants complained that they had been left out by the party and its candidate, Senator Ahmed Wadada.
## Background

The Rainbow Coalition brings together figures from the PDP and other parties who back Tinubu. Rivers governor Siminalayi Fubara has endorsed it, while Imo governor Hope Uzodimma, an APC leader, has rejected it in his state. Critics say it blurs party lines, while Wike says it puts the public interest first.
## What happens next
The coalition's role is expected to remain a point of tension within the APC and PDP as campaigning continues.
more: Wike urged FCT residents to mobilise votes for Tinubu.
Nasarawa APC says it is not part of the coalition.
Some members want a new campaign council.

stories.h: Atiku criticises Tinubu over retired police officers, promises pension reforms
stories.p: ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has reportedly accused the Tinubu government of neglecting retired police officers protesting over pensions. He promised to restore their gratuity and act on a police pension bill within 30 days if elected.
body: Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has criticised President Bola Tinubu over the treatment of retired police officers and unveiled what he called a Police Dignity Guarantee Plan.
## What he said

In comments reported on Monday, 2 November 2026, Atiku condemned what he described as the government's failure to protect retired officers who have been protesting at the National Pension Commission in Abuja over their pensions. He reportedly faulted the administration for not acting on a police exit bill which he said has been awaiting the President's signature since March 2026.
## His promises

Atiku said that if elected, he would restore gratuity for retired officers and implement a Police Pension Board Bill within 30 days of taking office. He said police officers who served the country deserve to retire with dignity.
## Background

Retired police officers have held repeated protests in Abuja over what they say are poor pensions under the contributory pension scheme, and have called for police to be removed from the scheme. The federal government has said it is working on reforms to improve welfare for serving and retired officers. Atiku has recently launched several attacks on the government's record, including accusing Tinubu of failing to keep his promises on electricity. The APC has dismissed such criticism, saying the government's reforms are beginning to show results.
## What happens next
The Presidency had not responded to Atiku's latest comments at the time of reporting.
more: Atiku says a police exit bill has been unsigned since March.
He promises to restore gratuity for retired officers.
He would act on a pension board bill within 30 days.

stories.h: National Assembly considering 74 extra seats reserved for women, says Senate leader
stories.p: Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele says lawmakers are considering a constitutional amendment to add 37 women-only seats each to the Senate and House of Representatives. The arrangement would last 16 years before a review.
body: The National Assembly is considering a constitutional amendment that would create 74 new legislative seats reserved for women, Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele has said.
## The proposal

Speaking on Monday, 2 November 2026, at a Law Week event organised by the Ekiti State branch of the International Federation of Women Lawyers, Bamidele reportedly said the plan would add 37 seats in the Senate and 37 in the House of Representatives, giving each state and the Federal Capital Territory one extra women-only seat in each chamber. He said the constitution review committee has also proposed three extra seats for women in each state house of assembly, and stressed that the new seats would be added to the existing ones rather than replacing any.
## How long it would last

Bamidele, who is vice-chairman of the Senate committee reviewing the 1999 Constitution, said the arrangement would run for 16 years, or four election cycles, before a full review. He described this as a sunset clause meant to allow a more inclusive political culture to develop.
## What happens next

Constitutional amendments need the approval of two-thirds of members of both chambers of the National Assembly and of at least 24 of the 36 state houses of assembly. Bamidele said the National Assembly was engaging state lawmakers to secure their support.
## Background

Women hold only a small share of seats in Nigeria's National Assembly, one of the lowest rates in Africa. A similar bill on special seats for women failed in 2022, which led to protests by women's groups. Supporters say reserved seats would give women a stronger voice in law-making, while critics argue they would add to the cost of governance.
more: The plan would add 37 women-only seats in each chamber.
State assemblies would get three extra seats for women.
The arrangement would run for 16 years before review.

stories.h: UK drops plan to make care workers wait 15 years for settlement
stories.p: UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has reportedly dropped a proposal that would have made some migrant care workers wait 15 years for indefinite leave to remain. Care workers who joined before May 2025 and earn at least £25,000 keep a five-year route, while most other lower earners face 10 years.
body: The UK government has reportedly dropped a plan that would have required some migrant care workers already in Britain to wait 15 years before they could settle permanently, a change that affects many Nigerians working in the sector.
## What changed

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood told the House of Commons on Monday, 2 November 2026, that care workers who joined the social care visa route before May 2025 and earn at least £25,000 a year in the sector will keep a five-year route to indefinite leave to remain. She also scrapped the proposed 15-year wait for other lower-paid workers, replacing it with a 10-year route.
## The new rules

Mahmood said settlement will now be more closely linked to a person's contribution, adding that the right to live in Britain must be earned. A five-year route will remain for people earning more than £50,000 a year and for qualifying workers in health and education. People earning more than £125,000 could settle in three years. Most other migrants, including those earning under £50,000, would face a 10-year route, while being able to renew their temporary visas.
## Why the plan was changed
The reversal followed opposition from Labour MPs, trade unions and migrant groups, who argued it was unfair to change the rules for people who came to Britain under different conditions.
## What it means for Nigerians

Nigerians are among the largest groups of overseas care workers recruited to the UK in recent years. Indefinite leave to remain allows a person to live, work and study in Britain without time limits and claim benefits where eligible, and is usually a step towards citizenship.
more: Care workers who joined before May 2025 keep a five-year route.
Most other lower earners face a 10-year route.
High earners above £125,000 can settle in three years.

stories.h: Actress Rachael Okonkwo shows off engagement ring, set to marry businessman
stories.p: Nollywood actress Rachael Okonkwo has shared a video showing her engagement ring and flowers, amid reports that she is set to marry Lagos businessman Chief Chukwudi Onuorah. Fans and colleagues have flooded her page with congratulations.
body: Nollywood actress Rachael Okonkwo, known to many fans as Nkoli Nwa Nsukka, is engaged, and her fans are celebrating with her.
## What happened

In a video shared on social media on Monday, 2 November 2026, the actress showed off her engagement ring and a bouquet of flowers, smiling and saying she was blushing and shy. Reports say she is set to marry Chief Chukwudi Onuorah, a businessman based in Lagos who has been described as a billionaire. Separate reports said friends of her partner had also gifted her ₦10 million, which she celebrated online.
## Background

Rachael Okonkwo rose to fame playing the character Nkoli Nwa Nsukka and has since appeared in many Nollywood films. The engagement comes during a busy period of celebrity weddings in Nigeria, including the recent Lagos wedding of singer LAX, which was attended by former President Goodluck Jonathan and his wife.
## How people reacted
Fellow actors and fans flooded her comments with congratulations and prayers for a happy marriage, while many asked when the wedding would take place.
## New government role

Days after the engagement, the actress announced that Enugu State governor Peter Mbah had appointed her Senior Special Assistant on Film and Creative Industry Development. She said the appointment was made in September but she chose to announce it later, and that she hopes to support emerging talent and filmmakers and help position Enugu as a destination for film, arts and culture.
## What happens next
The couple have not yet announced a wedding date.

stories.h: Francis Duru's family announces burial for 11 December in Imo
stories.p: The family of late actor Francis Duru has announced that he will be buried on 11 December in Isiala Mbano, Imo State. Services of songs will hold in Abuja on 25 November and in Imo on 10 December.
body: The family of veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru has announced his burial arrangements, weeks after he died at the age of 59.
## The arrangements

In a statement titled 'Forever in our hearts' posted on the actor's official Instagram page on Monday, 2 November 2026, the family said funeral events will begin with a service of songs and tributes in Abuja on Wednesday, 25 November, at 5pm at the Family Worship Center in Wuye. A second service of songs will be held on Thursday, 10 December, at his late father's family compound in Okai, Eziama, Isiala Mbano, Imo State. The funeral and burial will follow on Friday, 11 December, in the same community. The family added that branches and associations in various states are also organising their own services of songs.
## Background

Duru died on 22 October 2026 after an illness the family did not disclose. He was one of Nollywood's best-known faces from the 1990s and 2000s, starring in many popular films. His death led to tributes from colleagues across the industry. Last week, the family warned the public against fake burial flyers circulating online and said only official announcements should be trusted.
## How people reacted
Fans and colleagues shared tributes under the post and promised to attend the services.

stories.h: Governor Alex Otti opens Abia State facilities to opposition parties, says politics should not deny anyone access
stories.p: Abia State Governor Alex Otti says opposition parties should be allowed to use government-owned facilities in the state, including the stadium, as long as they follow due process and pay the required fees. He says he has already directed that no party be turned away because it is in opposition.
body: Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has made it clear that opposition political parties should be allowed to use government-owned facilities in the state, provided they follow the proper procedures and pay the required fees.
## The directive

According to the governor, he has already given instructions that no political party should be prevented from using public facilities, including the stadium, simply because it belongs to the opposition.
## A message of political tolerance

Otti's position sends an important message about tolerance and fairness. Government facilities are maintained with public resources, and access to them should not depend on which party someone supports.

This is one area where Nigerian politicians need to learn to separate governance from party politics. You can disagree with your opponents and campaign against them, and still respect their right to operate within the law.
Governor Otti appears to be making that distinction clear in Abia State.
## The big question
How many Nigerian governors would willingly allow opposition parties to use government facilities for their political activities?
Politics should never be an excuse to deny citizens their rights.

stories.h: Politics will shock you: Soludo's son seen promoting NDC song while his father backs Tinubu
stories.p: A Facebook video reportedly showing Ozonna Soludo, son of Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo, dancing to and promoting a song associated with the NDC has sparked reactions online. The NDC is linked in online discussions to Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, while Governor Soludo has reportedly been mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu.
body: Nigerian politics has taken another interesting turn, and this time the attention is on the family of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Charles Soludo.
## The video

A Facebook video reportedly showing Ozonna Soludo, the governor's son, dancing to and promoting a song associated with the NDC has sparked reactions online. In online discussions, the NDC has been linked to Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.
## Father and son in different camps?
What makes the situation interesting is the apparent political contrast between father and son.

While Ozonna appears to be enjoying a song associated with a different political camp, his father, Governor Soludo, has reportedly been mobilising political stakeholders in Anambra State in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.
## A dance is not a declaration
Dancing to a political song does not automatically mean someone has joined or endorsed a party. Ozonna has not made any confirmed political declaration through the video.

Even so, the moment has attracted attention because of his father's position. It is also a reminder that family ties do not necessarily decide political loyalty. A father may support one candidate while his son prefers another.
## The big question
If Governor Soludo is backing Tinubu while his son appears to be promoting a song associated with Obi and Kwankwaso, what does that say about the changing political atmosphere ahead of 2027?
Politics in Nigeria never stops surprising us.
